description: Signing in to Claude from the chat, on the machine the chat runs on: a turn of a Claude Code chat (or of Meta, which is a Claude Code session of this machine's) that fails for want of it (claude's sign-in ran out, was revoked, or isn't there) shows an amber-bordered card in place of its error, with Sign in; /login (or Sign in) runs claude auth login there and shows its progress in that card, and once it's signed in the failed turn can be sent again, with the attachments it had (what's attached since stays). This machine's chats sign in here; another machine's (and every chat on the phone) sign in by that machine's host process, through the mesh if that's how it's reached (the login request).
opens: /login (optionally with claude auth login's arguments) sent in the composer

A turn whose result is an error that signing in again would fix, or whose reply claude wrote in its place saying so (error authentication_failed, or text matching hostlogin.NEEDS_LOGIN: "Please run /login", "claude auth login", "Invalid API key", "OAuth token has expired", "Failed to authenticate", "Not logged in", "login … time limit / cannot be renewed", authentication_error, API Error: 401…); once a turn, live only (an old one in history keeps its red line); a Codex or pi chat's keeps its own error

decisions.said: (review of PR 423, the coordinator's decision) Meta runs under the default account, but its Sign in card signed in the CLI's own login, so a failed account sign-in couldn't be fixed from Meta
decisions.rule: Every app's Meta (Baude's and Record's) signs in, from its sign-in card, to the Claude account Meta runs under (this machine's default for Claude), as a chat's card does for the chat's account; the CLI's own sign-in only when that default is the CLI's own

decisions.said: (review of PR 420, the coordinator's decision) a profile chat's sign-in must replace that profile's token, not the CLI default's
decisions.rule: Every app's sign-in card, in a chat under a Claude token account (Session.account kind token), shows "Replace the token for <name>", why the turn failed, a password entry (the setup-token placeholder) and Save, which replaces that account's token on the chat's host and starts its claude again on it ("Token replaced"); claude auth login is never run for it

decisions.said: claude auth login with a profile dir should pre preferred over oauth.
decisions.rule: Every app's sign-in card, in a chat under a Claude folder account (Session.account kind folder), says "Sign in to <name> again" and why the turn failed; Sign in runs claude auth login on the chat's host with that account's folder (never the CLI's own sign-in), with the page's link and the code box the card has for any sign-in, then starts the chat's claude again on it

decisions.said:
Gracefully handle:
> "Failed to authenticate: this login reached its time limit and cannot be renewed. Run `claude auth login` to sign in again, or use `claude setup-token` and set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN for unattended jobs" -- I had to SSH into my compuetr to fix this
decisions.rule: Every app shows a Claude Code chat's turn that fails for want of a sign-in (one that ran out, including a login that reached its time limit) as the Sign in card in place of the error; Sign in runs claude auth login on the machine the chat runs on, through that machine's host for another machine's chats and the phone's, so no one has to log into that machine to recover

parts.name: card
parts.shows: Amber-bordered box (1px warning colour, 8px corners, 8px/12px padding): a bold title line, a line under it, then what can be done now. It's where the turn's error would be: that error's red line isn't drawn (nor the "turn ended with error" note).

parts.name: line
parts.shows: The stage's line (states): plain, dimmed (60%), or with a link.

parts.name: code row
parts.shows: While signing in (starting, the page's link): a text field filling the width, then "Send", "Cancel".

phone.does: The field fills a row of its own, with Send and Cancel in a row under it
phone.why: A phone's width leaves a field beside them too narrow to type a code in

actions.by: Enter in the field / click Send
actions.does: Passes the pasted code to claude auth login (on another machine: login_code); the line says "Checking the code…".
Stops the sign-in (on another machine: lets go of its connection, which stops it there).

parts.name: button
parts.shows: One accent button under the line, left-aligned: "Sign in" (not signed in), "Try Again" (failed, cancelled) or "Send again" (signed in, when the failed turn was sent from this window; gone once pressed).

actions.does: Starts claude auth login on the chat's machine; the card goes to starting.
Sends what the failed turn sent again, as your message (only when no turn is going and the box could send).

states.name: not signed in
states.shows: "Claude Code isn't signed in" (another machine's chat: "Claude Code on <host> isn't signed in") / dimmed the error's first sentence (at most 200 characters), and Sign in.

states.name: starting
states.shows: "Signing in to Claude…" / dimmed "Starting the sign-in…", and the code row.

states.name: the page's link
states.shows: This machine's: "A browser window should have opened to sign in. If it didn't, open the sign-in page." (the last words a link). Another machine's (its browser isn't here): "Open the sign-in page to sign in." (the first words a link, opened here). The code row stays.

states.name: checking
states.shows: Dimmed "Checking the code…" after a code is sent.

states.name: signed in
states.shows: "Signed in to Claude" / "as <account>" (or dimmed "claude auth status didn't say who as"), and Send again if there's a turn to send again. The chat's claude restarts on the new sign-in (after the turn if one runs): here, or stopped on its host so its next message starts it; the chat that failed, whichever's open by then.

states.name: failed
states.shows: "Sign-in didn't finish" / dimmed reason (what claude auth login said last, or why the machine couldn't be reached), and Try Again.

states.name: /logout
states.shows: Quiet notes: "signing out…" then "signed out of Claude" or "sign-out failed: <why>"; another machine's chat: "<host>'s claude signs out there: run claude auth logout on it".
